newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: 100,000 pay last respects to Sri Lankan politician.
newsitem.headline: 100,000 pay last respects to Sri Lankan politician.

text.p: An estimated 100,000 mourners in the southern Sri Lanka town of Ratnapura paid their last respects on Saturday to a politican gunned down earlier in the week.

Many mourners wept when the coffin of Nalanda Ellawala, 29, member of parliament from the ruling Peoples Alliance, was brought to the cremation site at Ratnapura, a gem-mining town 80 km (50 miles) southeast of Colombo.

Police estimated the crowd at 100,000 people. Ellawala was the youngest member of parliament and the scion of an influential political family in Ratnapura, the main town of a county with about 800,000 people.

About 300 orange-robed Buddhist monks chanted sutras and a Roman Catholic bishop also addressed his part of the service. The cremation ground was decked in white funeral flags and blue streamers for Ellawalas Sri Lanka Freedom Party, a major component of the Peoples Alliance coalition.

Before the service started under a blazing sun, police fired tear gas into a group of people which was refused entry into the funeral site, a large municipal sports ground opposite the Ratnapura town hall. Organisers later allowed them in.
Tuesdays killing of Ellawala during a roadside quarrel between his supporters and rivals of the main opposition United National Party (UNP) sparked two days of riots in Ratnapura.

Police named two suspects in the killing, UNP lawmaker Susantha Punchinilame and Mahinda Ratnatilleke, ex-UNP mayor of Ratnapura, and offered a reward of one million rupees ($17,500) to anyone providing information leading to their arrest.
"I call on all political parties to take action to prevent further violence," Speaker of Parliament K.B. Ratnayake said in his funeral oration.
In the riots on Tuesday and Wednesday, police said pro-Peoples Alliance mobs had set fire to homes and buildings of UNP supporters. No one was hurt in the riots.

Outside the cremation ground on Saturday, police fired tear gas to chase a crowd of about 300 people who hurled stones at the main Ratnapura police station. Army troops were called in and one solider was injured, but no one was arrested.
Several shops and kiosks were set on fire but there were no major clashes between rioters and security forces.
"We are just a convenient target for their anger and grief," one Ratnapura police official told reporters.
The funeral crowd slowly dispersed after family members lit the cremation fire. Police clamped an 8:00 p.m. curfew on the town.

Ellawalas killing came the day before a deadline for filing nominations in the March 21 local elections, the first electoral contest between the UNP and the Peoples Alliance since 1994 when the alliance ousted the UNP from 17 years in power.
More than 18,000 candidates from 12 political parties, including the alliance, the UNP and 132 independent groups, will take part in the polls for 238 local government assemblies.
The UNP suspended the party memberships of the two suspects, a day after party leader and former prime minister Ranil Wickremesinghe called on the two to turn themselves in.
